name: Planning a New Roof for Future Solar and ADU Projects in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: What should I ask a roofing contractor in Los Angeles to ensure my new roof stays compatible with future solar and potential ADU construction?
mainEntity.text: What should I ask a roofing contractor in Los Angeles to ensure my new roof stays compatible with future solar and potential ADU construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most roofing guides focus solely on materials and warranties, but if you plan to add solar or build an ADU over a garage or portion of your home later, choices made today can save or cost you thousands. When interviewing Los Angeles roofing contractors, explain your future plans clearly. Ask whether the existing roof structure can support likely solar panel and potential ADU loads, or if an engineer should verify. Request “solar-ready” features: clear pathways for conduit, attic access, and roof layouts that avoid unnecessary hips and valleys in the best solar exposure zones. Clarify fire rating and cool-roof requirements for your jurisdiction and how the selected materials will interact with solar mounts. If a garage or portion of the house may later become an ADU, discuss structural assumptions and water management now. You want flashing, drainage, and roofing seams placed with potential new walls or tie-ins in mind, minimizing cuts into a new roof. Ask for comprehensive as-built documentation—photos of flashing, underlayment, and penetrations—so future contractors can work without blindly opening your roofing system. Finally, confirm the roof warranty terms regarding future penetrations for solar or additions. Some manufacturers and installers require specific mounting systems or approved contractors to keep coverage intact.
acceptedAnswer.description: Confirm the roof structure can support future solar and possible ADU loads, ask for solar-ready conduit paths, verify fire and cool-roof compliance, and request detailed as-built photos. Discuss future penetrations, drainage, and framing zones to avoid placing critical seams or hardware where future solar rails or ADU tie-ins are likely.
